---
title: "Bayesian PROSPECT-D inversion in five probabilistic programming toolchains"
---

```{python}
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from _lib import *
F, P, V = read("fits.csv"), read("params.csv"), read("validation.csv")
fc = read("forward_check.csv")
fi = F[F["errmodel"] == "iid"]
present = [b for b in BACKENDS if b in set(fi["backend"])]
n_spec = fi["sample_id"].nunique()
```

This site compares **Bayesian inversion of the PROSPECT-D leaf radiative
transfer model** in five toolchains:

* **R + BayesianTools** (DEzs, base-R PROSPECT)
* **NIMBLE** (slice sampling, PROSPECT as a `nimbleFunction`)
* **Stan** (NUTS via CmdStan)
* **Julia / Turing.jl** (NUTS, ForwardDiff)
* **Python / PyMC** (NUTS, PyTensor)

Each toolchain has its own PROSPECT implementation, verified against a common
reference to machine precision. All five fit the same model to the same
leaves, so the comparison isolates the toolchain. The fits are checked against
measured leaf traits and against **held-out leaf transmittance**.

```{python}
ok = bool(fc[~fc["implementation"].str.startswith("reference")]["pass"].all())
eff = fi.groupby("backend")["min_ess_bulk_per_s"].median()
best = eff.idxmax() if len(eff) else None
cov = P[(P["errmodel"] == "iid") & P["param"].isin(["Cab", "Car", "Cw", "Cm"]) & P["measured"].notna()
        & (P["sample_id"] != "synthetic")]["covered90"].mean()
tiles = [
    ("Spectra fitted", f"{n_spec}", "10 LOPEX/ANGERS leaves + 1 synthetic"),
    ("Backends", f"{len(present)}", "same model, priors, data, inits"),
    ("Forward models agree", "✓ ≤ 1e-15" if ok else "✗ check", "vs. NumPy reference, both E₁ modes"),
    ("Most efficient", LABEL.get(best, "–"), f"median {eff.max():.1f} worst-param ESS/s" if best else ""),
    ("Measured traits inside 90% CI", f"{100*cov:.0f}%", "iid error model → over-confident"),
]
html = '<div class="stat-row">' + "".join(
    f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{a}</div><div class="value">{b}</div><div class="sub">{c}</div></div>'
    for a, b, c in tiles) + "</div>"
display(HTML(html))
```

## Headline comparison

```{python}
#| label: tbl-headline
#| tbl-cap: "Per backend, medians across spectra (iid error model, exact E₁). Setup is per fit: Stan's ~45 s compile happens once per model and is cached, so it shows as ~0 here. Relative trait error is the median of |posterior median − measured| / measured over Cab, Car, EWT and LMA. T is held-out transmittance."
rows = []
for b in present:
    f = fi[fi["backend"] == b]
    p = P[(P["backend"] == b) & (P["errmodel"] == "iid") & P["param"].isin(["Cab", "Car", "Cw", "Cm"])
          & (P["measured"] > 0) & (P["sample_id"] != "synthetic")]
    v = V[(V["backend"] == b) & (V["errmodel"] == "iid") & (V["region"] == "All") & (V["sample_id"] != "synthetic")]
    rows.append({
        "Backend": LABEL[b],
        "Sampler": {"stan": "NUTS", "pymc": "NUTS", "turing": "NUTS", "nimble": "AF slice", "bayestools": "DEzs"}[b],
        "Sampling time (s)": f["time_sampling_s"].median(),
        "Setup / compile (s)": f["time_setup_s"].median(),
        "Worst-param ESS/s": f["min_ess_bulk_per_s"].median(),
        "Max R̂": f["max_rhat"].max(),
        "Median rel. trait error": np.median(np.abs(p["q50"] - p["measured"]) / p["measured"]),
        "Trait 90% coverage": p["covered90"].mean(),
        "T RMSE": v[v["quantity"] == "T"]["rmse"].median(),
        "T 90% coverage": v[v["quantity"] == "T"]["coverage90"].median(),
    })
show_table(fmt_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), 3))
```

## Main findings

```{python}
bad = fi[fi["max_rhat"] > 1.05]
marg = fi[(fi["max_rhat"] > 1.01) & (fi["max_rhat"] <= 1.05)]
good_rh = fi[fi["max_rhat"] <= 1.01]["max_rhat"].max()
bad_desc = "; ".join(f"{LABEL[r.backend]} on {r.sample_id} (R̂ = {r.max_rhat:.2f})" for r in bad.itertuples())
exc = ("one exception" if len(bad) == 1 else f"{len(bad)} exceptions") + f": {bad_desc}"
marg_desc = ("; ".join(f"{LABEL[r.backend]} on {r.sample_id} reached R̂ = {r.max_rhat:.3f}" for r in marg.itertuples())
             + " (borderline; ESS is adequate)") if len(marg) else ""
eff_lo, eff_hi = eff.min(), eff.max()
slow = fi.pivot(index="sample_id", columns="backend", values="time_sampling_s")
thick = ["lopex_24", "an03r0271"]
nuts_ratio = (slow.loc[thick, ["stan", "pymc", "turing"]].mean() /
              slow.drop(index=thick + ["synthetic"])[["stan", "pymc", "turing"]].median()).mean()
```

1. **The toolchains recover the same posterior.** On every spectrum and
   parameter, posterior medians agree within Monte Carlo error (max R̂ =
   `{python} f"{good_rh:.3f}"`), and on the synthetic leaf all five recover the
   true parameters. There is `{python} exc`. One of BayesianTools' four DEzs runs got stuck, all 3
   of its internal chains together, at a much worse fit (σ ≈ 0.02 vs 0.007)
   on the white leaf, whose pigments sit near zero. Its other 9 chains agree
   with the NUTS and slice samplers. Separately, `{python} marg_desc`. See
   [Backends](backends.qmd).
2. **Efficiency differs more than accuracy.** The median worst-parameter
   ESS/s ranges from `{python} f"{eff_lo:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{eff_hi:.1f}"`.
   PyMC is fastest, then BayesianTools; Stan, Turing and NIMBLE are close
   together. The NUTS backends slow down about `{python} f"{nuts_ratio:.0f}"`×
   on the thickest, wettest leaves, where N, Cw and Cm are strongly
   correlated. The gradient-free samplers keep a fixed cost per iteration.
   Compilation and JIT time (Stan about 45 s once per model, NIMBLE about 45 s
   per fit, Julia about 15 s per session) matter for single-leaf workflows.
3. **Exact vs. approximate $E_1$ hardly matters.** The Swamee–Ohija closed form
   changes R and T by ≲ 8×10⁻⁴ and shifts posteriors by a fraction of a
   posterior SD. Its τ < 0 failure (k > 11.6) does occur in strong water bands,
   so it needs the usual clamp at 0. See [Forward model](verification.qmd).
```{python}
def cov_T(e):
    v = V[(V.backend == "stan") & (V.errmodel == e) & (V.region == "All") & (V.quantity == "T") & (V.sample_id != "synthetic")]
    return v["coverage90"].mean(), v["rmse"].mean()
def cov_trait(e):
    d = P[(P.backend == "stan") & (P.errmodel == e) & P.param.isin(["Cab", "Car", "Cw", "Cm"]) & P.measured.notna() & (P.sample_id != "synthetic")]
    return int(d.covered90.sum()), len(d)
ti, tr_i = cov_T("iid"), cov_trait("iid")
th, tr_h = cov_T("hetero_ar1"), cov_trait("hetero_ar1")
```

4. **The iid error model is the weak link, not the sampler.** Residuals are
   smooth, autocorrelated over tens of nm, several times the replicate noise,
   and shared across leaves. Under iid errors only
   `{python} f"{tr_i[0]}/{tr_i[1]}"` measured trait values fall inside the 90%
   intervals, and held-out transmittance coverage is
   `{python} f"{100*ti[0]:.0f}%"`. A heteroskedastic AR(1) likelihood (exact,
   $O(n)$) raises these to `{python} f"{tr_h[0]}/{tr_h[1]}"` and
   `{python} f"{100*th[0]:.0f}%"`, and also improves held-out T RMSE
   (`{python} f"{ti[1]:.3f}"` → `{python} f"{th[1]:.3f}"`). Its AR coefficient
   runs into φ → 1, though, which points to smoother GP or library-learned
   discrepancy models as the next step. See [Error models](error-models.qmd).
```{python}
Fa = read("fits.csv", main=False)
mv = Fa[Fa["backend"].isin(["pymc", "pymc-nutpie", "pymc-numpyro"]) & Fa["errmodel"].isin(["iid", "iid-fast", "iid-approx"])]
mm = mv.groupby(["backend", "errmodel"])["min_ess_bulk_per_s"].median()
py_base = mm.get(("pymc", "iid"), np.nan)
py_best_key = mm.idxmax() if len(mm) else ("pymc", "iid")
py_best = mm.max() if len(mm) else np.nan
lab_s = {"pymc": "pm.sample", "pymc-nutpie": "nutpie", "pymc-numpyro": "NumPyro"}
lab_e = {"iid": "exact", "iid-fast": "fast", "iid-approx": "Swamee–Ohija"}
py_best_lab = f"{lab_s[py_best_key[0]]} + {lab_e[py_best_key[1]]} E₁"
```

5. **PyMC can go faster without changing the model.** Replacing the default
   sampler and Cephes $E_1$ with `{python} py_best_lab` raises the median ESS/s
   from `{python} f"{py_base:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{py_best:.1f}"`
   (`{python} f"{py_best/py_base:.1f}"`×). The fast $E_1$ (NAG Chebyshev, ≤ 2×10⁻¹²
   error) helps every sampler. JAX's built-in `exp1` is very slow on CPU, and
   Swamee–Ohija is never the fastest choice. See [Faster PyMC](samplers.qmd).
6. **A bug fix along the way.** The PROSPECT-D `t21` in `rrtm` used the wrong
   refractive index; fixed in [ashiklom/rrtm#10](https://github.com/ashiklom/rrtm/pull/10).

## Reproducing

```bash
make data       # coefficient tables + validation spectra (needs ../RTM.jl, ../spectra_db)
make forward    # cross-language forward-model verification
make -j4 fits   # 5 backends x 11 spectra (+ Stan approx-E1 and hetero-AR(1) runs)
make summary    # results/summary/*.csv
make site       # render this site into docs/
```

Toolchain setup is in the repository README (`environment-r.yml`,
`environment-julia.yml`, `python/requirements.txt`, `julia/Project.toml`). The
earlier exploratory scripts are preserved on the
[`legacy-experiments`](https://github.com/ashiklom/prospect-inversion-comparison/tree/legacy-experiments)
branch.
